title: StripRequest
description: The trace annotations to remove from a codebase, on stdin. The off-ramp: adoption asks a consumer to write `verifies` traces into their own test sources, so the framework owes them a way to take those marks back — after off-boarding, or before re-adopting onto a corpus whose ids no longer mean what the marks say. CORE decides WHICH tokens go: it alone knows which RUs are active, so an adapter is never asked to judge whether a trace is stale. The adapter rewrites its own sources, because only it knows what an annotation looks like in its idiom.

checks.description: One entry per check whose annotation must change. A check absent from this list is left exactly as it is — the request is the complete instruction, so a stripper never sweeps on its own initiative.

id.description: The stack-qualified check id the scanner reported.

path.description: Consumer-root-relative source file, as the scanner reported it.

fn.description: The test's own name, so a stripper can locate the annotation without re-deriving the id.

remove.description: The exact trace tokens to drop from this check's annotation — RU ids, or the `infrastructure` token. Tokens the annotation carries but this list omits MUST survive: a test proving three requirements, one of them retired, keeps the other two. When nothing survives, the annotation itself goes, leaving no empty marker behind.
